Ben / team — attaching the artifacts we can share today. High-level notes included in the runbook. Where we couldn't provide raw ids (per security) we've redacted and replaced with hash digests and timestamps.

Attachments included (redacted):
- redwood_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 745KB) — one-page runbook + step checklist and verification channels
- dataflow-map-s3.png (PNG, 320KB) — annotated map showing tenant-scoped buckets, ephemeral caches, and snapshot boundaries
- erase-proofs-2026-05-20.zip (ZIP, 3.4MB) — contains: deletion-job-log.txt (redacted), snapshot-prune-records.csv (redacted), kms-audit-pointers.txt (lines with timestamp + event id)<

Key clarifications:
- Snapshots: For dedicated-region clusters we do not automatically replicate snapshots cross-region. On a tenant delete we trigger the snapshot-prune job which marks snapshots tied to the tenant and queues them for deletion; the prune job waits 48 hours to allow any escalation. We capture a deletion confirmation event and a verification hash.
- Backups: Automated backups are retained in-region by default for Dedicated; restoration workflows require region-local access and are not replicated unless explicitly configured by the customer (we note that in the runbook).
- KMS: We provide audit pointers (log entries with event ids and timestamps) showing key usage and key rotation events. We do not transmit KMS key material. If a customer requires HSM destruction proofs, that is provided as a separate attestation under an SCA/NDA.

Hannah
